newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may sell Furnas late '97, early '98 -Kandir.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may sell Furnas late '97, early '98 -Kandir.

text.p: Brazil may privatize its first federal power generator in late 1997 or early 1998 by selling Furnas, part of the Eletrobras holding company, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said Monday.

The government also expects to sell next year its remaining shares in recently privatized power distributor Light and to begin preparations for the sale of Brazil's telecommunications industry, he said in an interview.

"We're pressing ahead with the power sector with a view to next year selling the remaning shares in Light and perhaps prepare, not necessarily for next year -- it could be the end of 1997 or start of 1998 -- the privatization of Furnas," he said.
The sale of Furnas, one of four power generators owned by Eletrobras, would "produce an important result in terms of income," Kandir said. He declined to give a precise figure.
Furnas has installed capacity of 8.1 million kilowatts and generates power in several states, including the industrial powerhouses of Sao Paulo, Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro.

Eventually, Brazil intends to sell the other three Eletrobras generators -- Eletrosul, Eletronorte and CHESF -- but will not privatize the Itaipu hydroelectic project it shares with Paraguay nor the Furnas nuclear power plants.

Kandir said the sale of the federal power generators would benefit from the upcoming privatization of power companies owned by state governments. That would ease concern over distributors' ability to pay for the power they purchase.
The National Development Bank is working with several state governments to prepare their distributors for privatization.
